_note: background-service-account (dossiq fix after #3334). A cron job has no Nextcloud session, so OpenRegister sees Anonymous and refuses the write: the termijn reminder sweep (PauseChaseJob) sent its letter and then failed to store chasesSent, so the next run chased again. The sweep now writes as one Nextcloud account an admin picks (BackgroundServiceAccount, app config background_service_account), with OpenRegister's checks on, never with _rbac false. These are the schemas the sweep writes: deadlineInstance (chasesSent, lastChasedAt, chaseEscalatedAt) and termijnGebeurtenis (the chased and chase-escalated events). Each grants dossiq-background-service create and update. The block keeps what the open default allowed before: every logged-in user may create, read, update and delete, and an anonymous caller may read (public), so nothing changes for a handler or a portal read; it only names what the background account may do, which also holds once an operator turns on OpenRegister's enforce_default_closed. Admins keep OpenRegister's admin bypass. The case projection (pauseWaitingOn, chasesSent on the case) is deliberately not granted here: the case schema is default-open and central, so the account writes it as any logged-in user does. The repair step CreateBackgroundServiceGroup creates the group.
